newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 up yr/yr 26 percent at end-September.
newsitem.headline: China M2 up yr/yr 26 percent at end-September.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply rose by a year-on-year 26 percent at the end of September, the China Securities on Wednesday quoted central bank governor Dai Xianglong as saying.
Dai said M2 reached 7.2 trillion yuan at the end of September, the newspaper reported.

M1, currency in circulation plus current business deposits, rose by a year-on-year 15 percent to 2.7 trillion, Dai was quoted as saying. China has set a target of 18 percent annual growth for M1 for this year.
The official media quoted Dai as saying this week that broad M2 money supply fell by 2.69 percentage points year-on-year at the end of September.
Dai had said M2 growth was approaching the target of 25 percent annual growth set earlier this year.

MO money supply, or cash in circulation, rose by 11.8 percent year-on-year to the end of September, Dai said. Net currency put into circulation was expected to reach 120 billion yuan for the whole year.
